about.title: Gilroy Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Gilroy draws heavy foot traffic to its outlet shops, agricultural businesses, and Highway 101-adjacent retail centers, and with that traffic comes a steady number of slip, trip, and fall incidents on other people's property. These cases hinge on proving the property owner or manager knew, or reasonably should have known, about a spill, broken pavement, poor lighting, or a similar hazard and failed to address it. In Gilroy, that often means store aisles, parking lots along Monterey Highway, or apartment walkways. Because surveillance footage is frequently overwritten within days or weeks, and because memories fade quickly, early action matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law directly, but we can connect you with an attorney in our network who understands how Santa Clara County premises cases are built, from photographing the hazard to requesting video before it disappears. The consultation is free, and there's no fee unless the attorney recovers compensation for you.

whyChoose.title: Why Documentation Matters in Premises Cases

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California law requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and had time to fix or warn about it. An attorney can help gather maintenance logs, prior complaints, and other records that establish this.

items.title: Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Gilroy businesses recycle surveillance footage within days. Preserving that video quickly, before it's overwritten, can be critical to showing exactly how and why the fall happened.

items.title: Comparative Fault Affects Recovery
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by your share of responsibility but isn't eliminated just because you were partly at fault. An attorney can help present your case to minimize an unfair fault allocation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Gilroy?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the fall under California law, though claims against a public entity, like a city-owned sidewalk, have a much shorter deadline. It's best to consult an attorney promptly so critical deadlines aren't missed.

items.question: What should I do right after falling at a Gilroy store or business?
items.answer: If you're able, take photos of the hazard, the surrounding area, and your injuries before anything is cleaned up or fixed. Ask an employee to file an incident report and try to identify any witnesses, since these details can support a later claim.

items.question: Does it matter that Gilroy sees a lot of weekend foot traffic near Leavesley Road and 1st Street?
items.answer: Busy commercial corridors mean more visitors passing through stores and lots, which can increase spill or hazard exposure but doesn't change the legal standard. What matters is whether the property owner had notice of the specific hazard and failed to act on it.
